plugin.ghash.title: GHASH (GCM's hash over GF(2¹²⁸))
plugin.ghash.preset.mcgrew-viega-tc2: McGrew–Viega test case 2 – GHASH over C ‖ length block
plugin.ghash.preset.one-block-bits: One block, all 128 iterations of the multiplication
plugin.ghash.param.hHint: Exactly 16 bytes. In GCM, H = E_K(0¹²⁸), the block cipher applied to the all-zero block.
plugin.ghash.param.inputHint: 1 to 4 whole 16-byte blocks (16, 32, 48 or 64 bytes). In GCM: the padded AAD, the padded ciphertext and the length block.
plugin.ghash.param.detailHint: Per block shows one XOR and one multiplication per block. Per bit expands each multiplication into its 128 iterations (Algorithm 1).
plugin.ghash.region.x: Accumulator Y (X = Y ⊕ Bᵢ before the multiplication)
plugin.ghash.op.xorBlock: XOR the block into the accumulator
plugin.ghash.formula.ghash: Y₀ = 0, Yᵢ = (Yᵢ₋₁ ⊕ Bᵢ) • H in GF(2¹²⁸) mod x¹²⁸ + x⁷ + x² + x + 1
plugin.ghash.formula.mulBit.addReduce: x{{i}} = 1: Z{{next}} = Z{{i}} ⊕ V{{i}}; last bit of V{{i}} = 1: V{{next}} = (V{{i}} >> 1) ⊕ R
plugin.ghash.formula.mulBit.addShift: x{{i}} = 1: Z{{next}} = Z{{i}} ⊕ V{{i}}; last bit of V{{i}} = 0: V{{next}} = V{{i}} >> 1
plugin.ghash.formula.mulBit.skipReduce: x{{i}} = 0: Z{{next}} = Z{{i}}; last bit of V{{i}} = 1: V{{next}} = (V{{i}} >> 1) ⊕ R
plugin.ghash.formula.mulBit.skipShift: x{{i}} = 0: Z{{next}} = Z{{i}}; last bit of V{{i}} = 0: V{{next}} = V{{i}} >> 1
plugin.ghash.step.initial.block_one: GHASH hashes one 16-byte block under the hash subkey H = {{h}}. It starts with Y₀ = 0 and folds the block in: XOR it into Y, then multiply by H in the field GF(2¹²⁸).
plugin.ghash.step.initial.block_other: GHASH hashes {{count}} blocks of 16 bytes under the hash subkey H = {{h}}. It starts with Y₀ = 0 and folds in one block at a time: XOR it into Y, then multiply by H in the field GF(2¹²⁸). The last Y is the hash.
plugin.ghash.step.initial.bit_one: GHASH hashes one 16-byte block under the hash subkey H = {{h}}: Y₁ = (0 ⊕ B₁) • H. This view expands the multiplication into the 128 iterations of Algorithm 1: Z collects the product, V runs through H, H • x, H • x², …, and bit i of X decides whether V is added to Z.
plugin.ghash.step.initial.bit_other: GHASH hashes {{count}} blocks of 16 bytes under the hash subkey H = {{h}}: Yᵢ = (Yᵢ₋₁ ⊕ Bᵢ) • H with Y₀ = 0. This view expands each multiplication into the 128 iterations of Algorithm 1: Z collects the product, V runs through H, H • x, H • x², …, and bit i of X decides whether V is added to Z.
plugin.ghash.step.xorBlock: Block {{n}}: X = Y{{prev}} ⊕ B{{n}} = {{y}} ⊕ {{block}} = {{x}}. Adding in GF(2¹²⁸) is plain XOR.
plugin.ghash.step.multiply: Block {{n}}: Y{{n}} = X • H = {{x}} • {{h}} = {{y}}. The multiplication is in GF(2¹²⁸), reduced by x¹²⁸ + x⁷ + x² + x + 1.
plugin.ghash.step.mulBit.addReduce: Iteration {{i}}: bit {{i}} of X is 1, so V is added: Z = {{z}}. The last bit of V was 1, so V is shifted right by one and XORed with R: V = {{v}}.
plugin.ghash.step.mulBit.addShift: Iteration {{i}}: bit {{i}} of X is 1, so V is added: Z = {{z}}. The last bit of V was 0, so V is only shifted right by one: V = {{v}}.
plugin.ghash.step.mulBit.skipReduce: Iteration {{i}}: bit {{i}} of X is 0, so Z stays {{z}}. The last bit of V was 1, so V is shifted right by one and XORed with R: V = {{v}}.
plugin.ghash.step.mulBit.skipShift: Iteration {{i}}: bit {{i}} of X is 0, so Z stays {{z}}. The last bit of V was 0, so V is only shifted right by one: V = {{v}}.
plugin.ghash.step.mulBitLast.add: Iteration {{i}}, the last one: bit {{i}} of X is 1, so V is added. Z{{next}} = {{z}} is the product, so Y{{n}} = {{z}}.
plugin.ghash.step.mulBitLast.skip: Iteration {{i}}, the last one: bit {{i}} of X is 0, so Z does not change. Z{{next}} = {{z}} is the product, so Y{{n}} = {{z}}.
plugin.ghash.error.invalidParams: Give H and the input as hex text and choose a level of detail.
plugin.ghash.error.hLength: H has {{length}} bytes; it needs exactly 16.
plugin.ghash.error.inputLength: The input has {{length}} bytes; it needs 16, 32, 48 or 64 (1 to 4 whole 16-byte blocks).
plugin.ghash.error.detail: Unknown level of detail “{{detail}}”: choose per block or per bit.
